record.paper_title: Logical connections between some open problems concerning nil rings
record.original_question: If R is a nil ring, must the polynomial ring R[x] also be a nil ring?

evidence.quote: P6 If R is a nil ring, is R[x] also a nil ring?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A ring R (not necessarily with unit) is called nil if every element of R is nilpotent, i.e., for each r ∈ R there exists a positive integer n = n(r) such that r^n = 0. The polynomial ring R[x] consists of all polynomials in one commuting indeterminate x with coefficients in R, with the usual addition and multiplication.

Question: Does there exist a nil ring R such that the polynomial ring R[x] is not nil? Equivalently, is it true that for every nil ring R the polynomial ring R[x] is again nil?
artifact.status_search_result: This is Amitsur's question. It was answered in the negative by A. Smoktunowicz (Israel J. Math., 2000), who constructed a nil algebra R over any countable field such that R[x] is not nil. Thus there exist nil rings R with R[x] not nil.

status_evidence.title: Polynomial Rings over Nil Rings Need Not Be Nil
status_evidence.snippet: Smoktunowicz constructed a nil algebra over a countable field whose polynomial ring is not nil.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexample exists: nil R with R[x] not nil.

status_evidence.title: Agata Smoktunowicz - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Smoktunowicz constructed the first example of a nil algebra over a countable field such that the polynomial ring over the algebra is not nil.
